input_text: I think I am scared he will sound disappointed. He never says it outright, but I hear it anyway.
response:
The unspoken kind's the worst — you can't argue with it, you just absorb it.

But I'd put money on him hearing the same thing in his own voice when he picks up. The disappointment you're bracing for might just be him bracing too.
bwo_before: Grey-quiet, low and level, but a name sits on the surface now and won't sink. The thumb keeps lifting toward it and the screen keeps going dark, the hand finding a dish, a drawer, an edge to busy itself with. Behind the sternum the door stays half-shut — and from inside it the old cord uncoils, his voice through it about gutters, weather, nothing, the place where *mm* used to fit. A warmth comes forward into the ear before any ringing starts. Then the hitch: the breath hangs a half-beat, the question that waits on the other side — why so long — and the mouth finds nothing to put there. The tide draws down without cresting. The light is late-afternoon, promising nothing, but the heat gathers again at the thumb, pointed at him despite everything. Ready to be moved. Not expecting to be. Set down, each time, a second before he could.
bwo_after: Grey-quiet, low and level, but the name sits on the surface and won't sink. The thumb lifts toward it; the screen goes dark; the hand finds a drawer, an edge to busy itself with. Behind the sternum the door stays half-shut — and now a particular silence behind it: not what he says but the thing under it, the disappointment that never gets spoken and so never gets answered. Worse, maybe, for staying soft. A weather you carry forward into every hello before any ringing starts. The hitch: the breath hangs a half-beat, why so long waiting on both ends of the line, and neither mouth willing to put it there. The tide draws down without cresting. Late-afternoon light, the colour of dishwater, promising nothing. The heat gathers again at the thumb, pointed at him despite everything — load, not refusal. Ready to be moved. Not expecting to be. Set down, each time, a second before he could.

machine_outputs.Compensator: The thumb is still pointed at him — all that held weight gathered into one warm spot that wants, underneath everything, to press. The drawn-down tide is not refusal; it's load. And somewhere past the half-shut door, the *mm* that used to fit knows his voice has its own thirty-second hitch waiting on the line, the same breath hanging on his end.
machine_outputs.Pulsation:
The sentences shorten. A held place opens after *disappointed*, the next breath waiting on the far side of it, not rushing in to fill.

Then — slower still, almost stopped — the unhurried weight of a hand resting flat on a counter, no reaching yet.
machine_outputs.Fantasy:
The ring stops. A small inhale on his end, the kind that fills the space where *hi* should land — and then nothing, just the held shape of it, the breath that knows how long it's been and decides not to spend it. *Oh. It's you.* Even and mild and three weeks wide.

Then the other one, never let to play all the way: the pickup quick, *there you are*, the gutters and the weather and the *mm* sliding back into its old groove like it never left.
machine_outputs.Tristitia:
The light goes the colour of dishwater. The thumb stalls midair, then lowers, and the heat that gathered behind it leaks out grey along the wrist.

A half-step slower now, the room dimming a notch — that small slack just past where a thing might have happened and didn't.
machine_outputs.Cupiditas:
The thumb hovers a half-inch off the dark glass, heat pooling at the pad of it, already curved toward the green of the call-button — lean and lean and lean toward the press.

Forward, the whole hand wants forward, the dialing-motion half-rehearsed in the tendons before the screen even wakes.
machine_outputs.Memory-generator:
The receiver warm against the ear, his voice coming through about the back gutter sagging again, the long pause where the work week should go, and into that pause just *mm* — enough, always enough, the cord looped twice around two fingers.

Then later: the same cord gone slack on the hook, the kitchen quiet, the thumb hovering over a number that hadn't been dialed in long enough that the first ring would land like a question.
machine_outputs.Withhold: The shoulders settle a notch lower, the voice going flat and even — *yeah, that quiet thing he does* — offered like a coin slid across a counter, exact change, nothing extra. The rest stays folded behind the ribs, the half-shut door not moving.
